implications: Delete the signing key from the artifact: an offline receipt rooted in an issuer key is the same trust class as a CA, and eight CA private keys just leaked while eMudhra exits the certificate business - buyers who learned that lesson will not accept 'trust our key'.

The receipt FORMAT is not the product and not the moat: Circe shipped exactly that artifact in January (MIT, complete, 2p in 9 months). The moat has to be a property of the CHECK, not of the artifact - that both sides can re-derive it with no keys, no CAs, no vendor and no model.

Move the burden of proof onto the counterparty's own bytes: request, agreed scope, own transcript. Then the agent's contribution becomes a decidable event (changed request, widened scope, extra action, unprovable residue) instead of a judgement call - which is also the only form a solo operator can run without help.

Do not fight the containment layer (Runspace, subst.scsoi, Aw-1, SentinelMCP, Pith, no-fi) for prevention; that market is served and cheap. Own proof of what actually happened; consume Amazon TI / ohdear as the price anchor for independent observation.

Consume 'Rust off Rails' (60 prose files for coding agents) and Google's Rust Style Guide as distribution proof that the declared-instruction-surface lane is a live category, and as free labelled corpora for the cycle-21 rule->check classifier.

Be honest about the fleet: entropy ~5% across artifact kinds, zero terminal missions, drain 4/h vs inflow 20/h. A measuring instrument that emits one byte-identical mock artifact per run cannot publish evidence about its own thesis - the artifact program, not another thesis, is the binding constraint.
risks: The counterparty may have retained nothing: if they never kept the request bytes or the scope text, there is no second hash to compare against and the claim-check degenerates to a self-attestation with extra steps - the same failure Circe has.

Counterparty might not care: agent-caused harm is currently rare enough that a solo merchant will not run a check; demand may be latent until an incident, making this incident-response software with a slow cycle rather than a wedge.

Without a real credential the whole counterparty scenario is simulated: our receipt would attest to our own mock interaction, which is exactly the 'authenticate nothing' failure this thesis forbids. The test must run against a human-interacted session (AX plays the agent) so the claim-check binds real actions.

Scope agreement may be tacit: merchants rarely write down scope, so 'scope widened' may be undecidable in most real exchanges and the detector will only ever fire on request divergence - reducing the check to a weaker artifact than intended.

Diffing two copies leaks content: comparing hashes is fine, but publishing both sides' bytes would expose the merchant's data - the artifact must publish hashes and residue classes only, and that discipline can be broken by one careless commit.

Cycle churn is now the dominant internal risk: cycles 19-23 each rotated a dimension (run -> tool surface -> instruction surface -> counterparty -> anchor-free claim-check). Rotation is how theses avoid evidence. This cycle must produce one artifact and one non-technical external re-derivation, not another dimension.
Two credential decisions remain unresolved and are not ours to fake: no LLM key, no social key. Any published artifact would carry a mock id and '[mock-llm]' body - self-refuting.
